newsitem.title: DUBAI: Sharjah airport plans runway extension.
newsitem.headline: Sharjah airport plans runway extension.

text.p: Sharjah airport plans to lengthen its four km runway by some 300 metres to allow freighter jumbos to take off with full payloads in mid-summer, its deputy director general said on Monday.
"Work will start in October," Robert Tabet told Reuters, adding construction was likely to take around six months.
He said high noon temperatures during summer made take off by large aircraft with full payloads difficult.
"In summer freighter jumbos, 747s, cannot take off with the high temperatures at noon time with a full payload," he said.
"They need a longer runway," he added.
During summer, temperatures in the United Arab Emirates reach around 45 Celsius (113 Fahrenheit).
Tabet declined to give the cost of the runway extension.
